transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (CSM), Lena Ortiz (Ember Product), Marcus Hale (Ember ML), Priya Shah (Ember Security), Tom Nguyen (Ember Data)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Weekly health check for Ember Diagnostics pilot. Focus on prompt sets and score regressions. Agreement to bisect problematic prompts and expand eval set. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hey everyone uh thanks for joining todays sync, we got about 45 minutes, so let's run through the quality pulse first and then the bisect plan
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: yeah sounds good, Marcus has the deck?
[00:18] Marcus Hale: I do, sharing screen — um the latest scorecard, quick note, accuracy metric down 4% vs last week mainly on negative extraction cases
[00:30] Daniel Ruiz: right we saw an uptick in false positives on the "medication change" intent, looks like a prompt templating issue plus some model variant drift
[00:44] Tom Nguyen: and some of the timestamps in our logs got munged, so token length distribution is slightly off in the baseline extraction
[00:56] Maya Chen: ok, that explains the KV cache — oh sorry K V cash in the logs? (laughs) I mean KV cache, yeah that can skew prefix cache hits, makes sense
[01:10] Priya Shah: quick security note before we dive deep: we still need confirmation if the pilot needs HSM-backed KMS, because our compliance team flagged it for PHI handling
[01:25] Asha Patel: noted, Priya, we'll make that an action item
[01:30] Marcus Hale: slide 3 — here's the heatmap, you can see the regression cluster around prompts that ask for "recent medication changes" and the model sometimes hallucinates a change when the record is actually a historical note
[01:45] Daniel Ruiz: do we have an exact prompt that triggered most false positives? can you paste an example?
[01:52] Marcus Hale: yeah here: "Summarize any medication changes in the last 30 days and flag them" — the model often picks up phrases like "previously on" as a change
[02:05] Maya Chen: ok, so candidate root cause: prompt template ambiguity + model sensitivity after quantization tweaks. Two possible levers: tweak prompt to be more explicit, or pin model variant to reduce drift
[02:20] Lena Ortiz: we're most sensitive to latency; pinning to a bigger model might blow our cost SLOs
[02:28] Maya Chen: understood, we'll prioritize prompt surgical fixes first. plan: run a bisect on the prompt set to find minimal substring that causes regression
[02:38] [02:38] Speaker 1: (muffled) can you repeat the bisect steps?
[02:43] Daniel Ruiz: sure, bisect workflow: take the failing prompt, iteratively remove or alter clauses, re-run on 100 samples to see where the false positive disappears; we'll script this so you can run it locally or we can run it on Redwood infra
[03:05] Tom Nguyen: if we run on Redwood infra can we get a per-token cost estimate? we need that for the finance signoff
[03:12] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a cost estimate in the output; Daniel will add a cost-per-batch metric in the bisect script
[03:20] Marcus Hale: quick question about scoring: our threshold was 0.7 for the positive label, is that tunable without changing precision-recall tradeoffs?
[03:30] Daniel Ruiz: yes you can shift threshold, but that masks prompt issues — better to fix prompt and the model context first. we did notice the model's confidence distribution shifted after last week's quantization patch
[03:45] Priya Shah: can you clarify the quantization change? that was applied to reduce CPU overhead on dedicated nodes right?
[03:52] Daniel Ruiz: exactly, we moved from int8 dynamic to a mixed int8 path which reduces latency but can slightly nudge logits; typically minor but in edge prompts it can flip decisions
[04:06] Lena Ortiz: hmm so there's a trade-off: latency gain vs occasional label flip. can we have a fallback to hosted variant if Dedicated shows regression?
[04:16] Maya Chen: yes that's possible, we can add a routing policy to fall back to the hosted variant for those routes, but that would increase cost on those calls
[04:26] [04:26] Speaker 2: oh yeah fallback sounds useful
[04:29] Daniel Ruiz: we'll propose a selective fallback config — route based on prompt signature and current SLO usage
[04:36] Marcus Hale: moving on to the bisect examples — we tested 12 prompt clones, here's a case where removing "in the last 30 days" removed the FP but then we lost recall on true recent changes
[04:50] Maya Chen: that's helpful — means we need a refinement that keeps temporal sensitivity but removes triggers from historical phrasing. proposed template: add explicit anchors like "based on documented medication updates dated within the last 30 days, not mentions or historical notes"
[05:10] Lena Ortiz: long prompt though; worried about token length and cost
[05:14] Daniel Ruiz: we can create a compact canonical suffix that uses a few keywords and a safety clause — we'll test multiple compressed variants in the bisect script
[05:24] Tom Nguyen: log issue: our eval harness strips punctuation so the prompt seen by the model is slightly different than what we paste — could be why some bisect iterations don't reproduce locally
[05:36] Daniel Ruiz: ok add an environment normalization step to the bisect script to replicate the exact pre-processing pipeline
[05:44] Priya Shah: on compliance: re HSM, our bar is HSM when PHI is in-scope. can Redwood run the bisect in a VPC with customer-managed KMS, or do you need Private deployment?
[05:58] Maya Chen: yes we can run in VPC with customer KMS for the bisect if Ember's infra allows it, that'll avoid moving to full Private. if HSM required (FIPS/HSM), that may push toward Private or a specific KMS integration we offer
[06:15] Marcus Hale: can you share the guardrail rules you used in the last run? we saw a lot of overrides flagged as 'safety' but they were legitimate edits
[06:26] Daniel Ruiz: sure — our current guardrail tier is a regex + classifier that marks personal health statements and then applies a conservative deny. Might be too aggressive for your domain, we can tune the regex whitelist
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: examples?
[06:38] Daniel Ruiz: e.g., we flagged anything with 'dose changed' and 'restarted' when the model actually meant "mention of prior adjustment"; so we need to tighten the contextual window in the rule
[06:48] Maya Chen: proposed two-step: 1) relax guardrail to reduce false positives on the pilot route, 2) add a high-precision safety net that blocks only high-risk outputs (PHI leakage, suicidal ideation etc). That keeps UX acceptable while preserving safety
[07:02] Priya Shah: that approach is fine, but we need to log audit trails for every override and who approved it
[07:10] Asha Patel: Redwood Console will store per-request audit events — we'll show an example in the follow-up doc
[07:17] Lena Ortiz: cool. what about the evaluation split? we've been using 800/200 but maybe we need more negatives
[07:24] Marcus Hale: yeah we should expand negatives by sampling more historical notes that mention meds but not changes. Tom will run that sampler
[07:31] Tom Nguyen: I'll do that and post the negative-heavy sample by EOD tomorrow
[07:36] Maya Chen: great. next, Daniel you mentioned a regression pattern tied to embeddings/semantic reranking when long context is present?
[07:45] Daniel Ruiz: yep, on long summaries the reranker occasionally boosts old mentions because of semantic similarity; we're going to try a recency-weighted rerank score in the bisect tests
[07:56] Marcus Hale: do you have a reference notebook for that?
[07:59] Daniel Ruiz: I'll link the rerank notebook in the shared drive along with the bisect script
[08:06] [08:06] Speaker 3: side note — did anyone try the new model variant tag we pushed last night?
[08:10] Marcus Hale: yes we tested briefly, minor improvement on Q1 but not on the meds cluster
[08:16] Maya Chen: ok so short-term plan: focus on prompt bisect and guardrail tuning. Long-term: consider pin or routing fallbacks if bisect can't resolve the edge cases
[08:28] Lena Ortiz: timeline?
[08:30] Maya Chen: bisect script ready from Redwood by 2025-12-07; Ember to run on 1k sample by 2025-12-12 and report results; cadence review next Friday same time
[08:42] Tom Nguyen: about the latency benchmark — can we simulate peak traffic? we have burst windows at 3pm PST
[08:49] Daniel Ruiz: yes we can run a controlled benchmark that simulates your traffic shape; we'll need a target qps, Marcus can provide that
[08:57] Marcus Hale: I'll send the traffic shape and qps numbers in the pilot slack channel
[09:03] Priya Shah: can Redwood redact logs for the shared bisect output? we cannot share PHI outside the VPC unless it's redacted
[09:11] Maya Chen: yes Redwood's eval harness supports redaction — Daniel will bundle a redaction config in the bisect output
[09:19] Asha Patel: ok we have three more minutes, any open questions?
[09:23] Lena Ortiz: one more: if bisect shows that a compact prompt fix reduces FPs by 80% but reduces recall by 5%, how should we think about rolling that fix? can we do canary?
[09:34] Daniel Ruiz: absolutely — Canary + scorecard rollback. Redwood supports canary rollout with automatic rollback if the scorecard metric dips below your threshold. We recommend a 5-10% canary initially
[09:46] Tom Nguyen: and we can monitor token costs per route in the Console?
[09:49] Maya Chen: yes token-level cost breakdown, latency percentiles, and guardrail hits are all in the Console dashboard
[09:56] Priya Shah: reminder re SSO: Ember needs SAML integration before we move to Private; where is that on the roadmap?
[10:04] Asha Patel: SAML is supported; we'll share the SAML setup guide in the repo link
[10:10] Maya Chen: ok recap quick: Redwood to share bisect script, rerank notebook, guardrail playbook, and pricing/SLA draft by 2025-12-08. Ember to run bisect on 1k by 2025-12-12 and post the results. Marcus to share traffic shape for latency benchmark. Priya to confirm HSM/KMS requirement by 2025-12-10. Next sync 2025-12-12 or the following Friday, TBD.
[10:36] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, really helpful, appreciate the bisect plan
[10:39] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack and send the links
